comparator.name: Religious Studies
comparator.route: Cultural and Political Impact of Religion specialisation with University Minor
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official programme page accounts for a complete 180-EC bachelor. Years 1 and 2 each contain eight compulsory 7.5-EC courses. Year 3 contains a genuine 30-EC minor or equivalent open external study space, one 7.5-EC specialisation course, the 7.5-EC Thesis Seminar, the 10-EC Bachelor Thesis and 5-EC Science Communication. The Cultural and Political Impact of Religion specialisation is selected under the broad-academic-identity rule because the official programme description centrally emphasises religion in contemporary social and political questions; this choice is independent of UCR fit. The 30-EC University Minor is preserved as open choice space rather than populated with invented courses.

routeSelection.route: Cultural and Political Impact of Religion specialisation with University Minor
routeSelection.basis: The current generic Religious Studies bachelor offers a flexible third year with a 30-EC minor and named specialisation options. Cultural and Political Impact of Religion best represents the programme page’s broad emphasis on religion in contemporary society, politics, conflict, migration and sustainability; the University Minor preserves the programme’s genuine open choice space. The route is selected independently of UCR fit.

exception.reason: The Groningen bachelor is defined by sustained disciplinary study of Christianity, Judaism, Islam, Hinduism, Buddhism and indigenous South Asian traditions; comparative Religious Studies concepts and methods; anthropology, psychology and sociology of religion; ritual; sacred images and texts; religion, media, identity and politics; a dedicated specialisation; and a Religious Studies thesis. UCR has relevant courses in philosophy, sociology, politics, history, archaeology, literature, media and cultural analysis, but no course or sequence in Religious Studies, theology, comparative religion, sacred texts, lived religion or the history and practice of religious traditions. A 24-course UCR programme could examine culture, ideas and institutions around religion, yet most courses would treat religion only incidentally and would omit the target’s defining disciplinary core. Publishing it as a closest match would therefore misstate what UCR teaches.
exception.curriculumContext: The current official programme page establishes 60 EC in each year and a coherent 180-EC pathway. The 30-EC third-year minor is preserved as genuine open space. One current 7.5-EC specialisation is selected neutrally, followed by the required Thesis Seminar, 10-EC Bachelor Thesis and Science Communication.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 records in the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx (SHA-256 7bf6c2ae9de0837086ec741c27bd94ed7e85dff2d25bde619ecd50cc4d685879), including names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned availability. GOSPHIL111 Introduction to Western Philosophy, GOSPHIL212 Ethics, GOSSOCI111 Introduction to Sociology, GOSSOCI214 Modern Sociology, GOSPOLI111 Introduction to Political Philosophy, GOSHIST111 Modern History and GOSSOCI212 Qualitative Research Methodology support historical, philosophical and social-scientific inquiry. MCCHEAM112 Introduction to World Archaeology, MCCHEAM211 African Art & Heritage, MCCHEAM212 Renaissance Italy & Global Mediterranean, MCCHEAM315 Heritage & Ancient Democracy, MCCLITR112 Great Literary Works and MCCLITR211 World Myth & Literature include limited religious, Islamic or mythic material. GOSLAWJ213 Comparative Constitutional Law considers religious constitutions, and GOSPHIL214 Philosophy of Mind briefly includes Buddhist philosophy. None studies religion as the disciplinary object or provides comparative-religion, sacred-text, ritual, theology, lived-religion or Religious Studies research training. These adjacent courses cannot form a substantively honest 24-course closest-match degree.
